zh: 初，明帝為王，始納河內虞氏為妃，帝即位，虞氏不得立為后，太皇后卞太后慰勉焉。
literal: At first, when Emperor Ming was a prince, he first took Lady Yu of Henei as consort; when he ascended the throne Lady Yu could not be established as empress, and Grand Empress Dowager Bian comforted and encouraged her.
idiomatic: When Ming-di was still a prince he first took Lady Yu of Henei as consort. Once he took the throne she could not be made empress, and Grand Empress Dowager Bian tried to console her.

zh: 虞氏曰：「曹氏自好立賤，未有能以義舉者也。
literal: Lady Yu said, "The Cao house has always liked to elevate the base; none has ever been raised on grounds of righteousness.
idiomatic: Lady Yu replied, "The Cao clan has always favored elevating the lowborn; none has ever been raised on grounds of righteousness.

zh: 然后職內事，君聽外政，其道相由而成，苟不能以善始，未有能令終者也。
literal: Yet the empress manages inner affairs and the lord listens to outer government; their way is mutually completed thereby; if one cannot begin well, none has ever been able to finish well.
idiomatic: Yet the empress governs within while the sovereign rules without, and the two must work together. If the beginning is not good, the end is never good.

literal: This will surely be how the state is lost and the sacrifices cut off!"
idiomatic: This is surely how a realm loses its altars and its line!"

literal: Lady Yu then withdrew with a black headband and returned to the palace at Ye.
idiomatic: Lady Yu then put on mourning dress and withdrew to the palace at Ye.

zh: 進嘉為奉車都尉，曾騎都尉，寵賜隆渥。
literal: Jia was promoted to Commandant of the Imperial Carriage and Zeng to Cavalry Commandant, with favor and gifts rich and generous.
idiomatic: Mao Jia was promoted to commandant of the imperial carriage and Mao Zeng to cavalry commandant, with lavish favor and gifts.

zh: 頃之，封嘉博平鄉侯，遷光祿大夫，曾駙馬都尉。
literal: Before long Jia was enfeoffed as Marquis of Boping Village and transferred to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness; Zeng was made Commandant of the Stable for the Son-in-Law.
idiomatic: Soon Mao Jia was enfeoffed as Marquis of Boping village and made grand master for splendid happiness; Mao Zeng became commandant of the stable for the son-in-law.

zh: 嘉本典虞車工，卒暴富貴，明帝令朝臣會其家飲宴，其容止舉動甚蚩騃，語輒自謂「侯身」，時人以為笑。
literal: Jia had originally been overseer of the Yu clan's carriage craftsmen and suddenly became rich and noble; Emperor Ming ordered court ministers to gather at his home for drink and feast; his bearing and movements were very crude and foolish, and in speech he constantly called himself "this marquis's person"; people of the time took it as a joke.
idiomatic: Jia had once overseen the Yu family's carriage workshops and suddenly shot to wealth and rank. Ming-di had court ministers feast at his house, where his manners were oafish and he kept calling himself "the marquis's own person"—a laughingstock at the time.

zh: 孫盛曰：古之王者，必求令淑以對揚至德，恢王化於關雎，致淳風於麟趾。
literal: Sun Sheng states: The kings of antiquity necessarily sought worthy and virtuous consorts to respond to and display supreme virtue, extending kingly transformation through Guanju and bringing pure custom through Linzhi.
idiomatic: Sun Sheng writes: Ancient kings sought worthy consorts to answer and display supreme virtue, spreading royal civilizing power through Guanju and pure custom through Linzhi.

zh: 及臻三季，並亂茲緒，義以情溺，位由寵昏，貴賤無章，下陵上替，興衰隆廢，皆是物也。
literal: When the three later ages were reached they all disrupted this thread: righteousness drowned in emotion, rank came through favor and folly, noble and base lacked distinction, the lower encroached and the upper declined, rise and fall, flourishing and ruin—all were the same thing.
idiomatic: By the three later ages that thread was ruined everywhere: duty drowned in passion, rank won through blind favor, noble and base confused, inferiors overrunning superiors—rise and fall alike followed the same pattern.

zh: 魏自武王，暨於烈祖，三后之升，起自幽賤，本既卑矣，何以長世？
literal: From King Wu of Wei down to the Fierce Ancestor, the elevation of three empresses all began from obscure and base origins; the root was already low—how could the line endure long?
idiomatic: From Cao Cao down to Cao Pi, three empresses were raised from obscure and humble origins. With so low a foundation, how could the house endure for ages?

zh: 詩云：「絺兮绤兮，淒其以風。」
literal: The Odes say, "Fine and coarse linen—how chill it is in the wind."
idiomatic: The Odes say, "Fine and coarse linen—how chill it is in the wind."

literal: Is this not what is meant!
idiomatic: Is this not exactly what is meant!

zh: 后又加嘉位特進，曾遷散騎侍郎。
literal: Later the empress again added for Jia the position of Special Advance, and Zeng was transferred to Attendant Gentleman at the Palace.
idiomatic: The empress later gave Mao Jia the rank of special advance and moved Mao Zeng to attendant gentleman at court.

zh: 青龍三年，嘉薨，追贈光祿大夫，改封安國侯，增邑五百，並前千戶，諡曰節侯。
literal: In the third year of Qinglong Jia died; he was posthumously granted Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Anguo, given five hundred added households making one thousand together with prior holdings, and honored with the posthumous title Marquis Jie.
idiomatic: In Qinglong 3 Mao Jia died. He was posthumously made grand master for splendid happiness, re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Anguo with five hundred added households for a total of one thousand, and given the posthumous title Marquis Jie.

zh: 四年，追封后母夏為野王君。
literal: In the fourth year the empress's mother Xia was posthumously enfeoffed as Mistress of Yewang.
idiomatic: In the fourth year the empress's mother Xia was posthumously enfeoffed as lady of Yewang.
